_meta.description: Normal-approximation 95% confidence interval for the mean of customers.pulse income via AGG_CI_LOWER + AGG_CI_UPPER (paired with AGG_AVERAGE for the centre point). Params.confidence defaults to 0.95 when omitted; Params.method defaults to "normal" (the streaming-friendly z-quantile path; "bootstrap" is reserved for a buffered follow-up). Streamable — the CI bounds ride alongside Welford state.
_meta.interpretation: The mean income sits in the middle of a fairly tight interval: each bound lies within about a tenth of the mean, so the cohort pins the typical income down well. The interval describes the mean, not individual customers, whose incomes spread far more widely.
_meta.name: confidence_interval_normal
_meta.question: What is a typical customer's income, and how precisely does this cohort pin it down?
